references.text: Parallel account where the Israelites admit their sin and decide to go up to the mountain to fight, despite the Lord's warning.
Moses reminds the people how they were disobedient and presumptuously went up into the mountain.
The immediate continuation showing the consequence of their presumption—they were defeated by the Amalekites and Canaanites.
Moses' warning against going up, because the Lord was not with them—the context showing that their action was disobedience.
Uses the same expression 'rose early in the morning' (וַיַּשְׁכִּמוּ בַבֹּקֶר) to describe an act of obedience, in contrast to this disobedient act.
The book of Hebrews refers to the wilderness journey narrative as a warning against unbelief and disobedience toward God's promises.
